paite: Huan, TOUPA'N Mosi leh Aron a houpih a,
english: Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying to them,

paite: Israel suante houpih unla, Leitung a gamsa tengteng lak a na nek ding uh thilhingte hiai ahi.
english: “Speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘These are the living things which you may eat among all the animals that are on the earth.

paite: Gamsa lak a chin ka, chin ka paisuak, eknel hai chi peuhmah na ne thei ding uh.
english: Whatever parts the hoof, and is cloven-footed, and chews the cud among the animals, that you may eat.

paite: Himahleh eknel hai hiam, chin ka paisuak hiam lak ate hichibangte zaw na nek ding uh ahi kei; sangawngsau, eknel hai leleng, a chin a kak louh ziak in; nou ding in a nin ahi.
english: “‘Nevertheless these you shall not eat of those that chew the cud, or of those who part the hoof: the camel, because he chews the cud but doesn’t have a parted hoof, he is unclean to you.

paite: Huan, zupi, eknel a hai na a, a hihhang in a chin a kat louh ziak in; nou ding in a nin ahi.
english: The coney, because he chews the cud but doesn’t have a parted hoof, he is unclean to you.

paite: Huan, zusapi, eknel a hai na a, a hihhang in a chin a kat louh ziak in, nou ding in a nin ahi.
english: The hare, because she chews the cud but doesn’t part the hoof, she is unclean to you.

paite: Huan, vok, a chin a ka a, a ka paisuak na a, a hihhang in eknel a hai louh ziak in; nou ding in a nin ahi.
english: The pig, because he has a split hoof, and is cloven-footed, but doesn’t chew the cud, he is unclean to you.

paite: A sa uh na ne ding uh ahi kei, a luang uh leng na khoih ding uh ahi kei, nou ding in a nin ahi.
english: Of their flesh you shall not eat, and their carcasses you shall not touch; they are unclean to you.

paite: Tui sung a teng tengteng ah hiaite na ne thei ding uh: tuipite, luite, tui a om khate leh lipte nei photphot na ne thei ding uh.
english: “‘These you may eat of all that are in the waters: whatever has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas, and in the rivers, that you may eat.

paite: Tui sung a teng tengteng leh tui a thil hing om tengteng lak ah tuipi ate, lui ate, khate leh lipte neilou photphot zaw, nou ding in thil kihhuai ahi a,
english: All that don’t have fins and scales in the seas, and in the rivers, of all that move in the waters, and of all the living creatures that are in the waters, they are an abomination to you,

paite: Nou ding in thil kihhuai ahi ding ua; a sa uh na ne ding uh ahi kei, a luangte uh thil kihhuai a na neih ding uh ahi.
english: and you detest them. You shall not eat of their flesh, and you shall detest their carcasses.

paite: Tui a khate leh lipte neilou photphot zaw nou ding in thil kihhuai ahi.
english: Whatever has no fins nor scales in the waters, that is an abomination to you.

paite: Huan, vasa lak ah hiaite thil kihhuai a na neih ding uh ahi; nek ding ahi kei hi, thil kihhuai ahi uh: muvanlai, musane leh tuivapi,
english: “‘These you shall detest among the birds; they shall not be eaten, they are an abomination: the eagle, and the vulture, and the black vulture,

paite: Muvompi, musi a chi himhimte;
english: and the red kite, any kind of black kite,

paite: Va-ak chiteng a chi himhimte;
english: any kind of raven,

paite: Simbu, vabak, tuipi vasate, mu chi himhim;
english: the horned owl, the screech owl, and the gull, any kind of hawk,

paite: Simbutanglip, ngagal, simbupi,
english: the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,

paite: Tuivapi, vabukngak, musanepi,
english: the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,

paite: Inntungva, dil vasa a chi himhim, huihtun leh bakte.
english: the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.

paite: Kha nei khe li a pai chi peuhmah nou ding in thil kihhuai ahi.
english: “‘All flying insects that walk on all fours are an abomination to you.

paite: Himahleh kha nei, khe li a pai chi leng leitung a tawmna ding a a khezung tung lam ua khe nei tengteng lak ah hiaite na ne thei ding uh;
english: Yet you may eat these: of all winged creeping things that go on all fours, which have legs above their feet, with which to hop on the earth.

paite: Hiaite leng na ne thei ding uh: khau a chi himhim, ekkhingne khaupe a chi himhim, khuangbai a chi himhim leh khaupe a chi himhimte.
english: Even of these you may eat: any kind of locust, any kind of katydid, any kind of cricket, and any kind of grasshopper.

paite: Himahleh kha nei, khe li nei, a pai a pai photphot nou ding in thil kihhuai ahi vek hi.
english: But all winged creeping things which have four feet, are an abomination to you.

paite: Huan, hiaite ziak in na buah ding uh: kuapeuh, sa luang khoih peuhmah nitak lam tan in a buah ding ua;
english: “‘By these you will become unclean: whoever touches their carcass shall be unclean until the evening.

paite: Huan, kuapeuh huai luang lami peuhmah in a puante uh a sawp ding uh ahi, nitak lam tan in a buah ding uh.
english: Whoever carries any part of their carcass shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening.

paite: Gamsa chin ka a, ka paisuaklou, eknel leng hailou chi tengteng nou a ding in thil nin ahi a; kuapeuh huaite khoih a nin ding uh.
english: “‘Every animal which parts the hoof, and is not cloven-footed, nor chews the cud, is unclean to you. Everyone who touches them shall be unclean.

paite: Huan, bok a pai tengteng lak a khebom a pai peuhmahte nou ding in thil nin ahi a; a luang uh khoih peuhmah nitaklam tan in a nin ding uh.
english: Whatever goes on its paws, among all animals that go on all fours, they are unclean to you. Whoever touches their carcass shall be unclean until the evening.

paite: Huan, a luang lami peuhmah in a puante uh a sawp ding uh ahi, nitaklam tan in a nin ding ua; nou ding in thil nin ahi.
english: He who carries their carcass shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening. They are unclean to you.

paite: Huan, lei a a vak a vakthoh chi lak a nou ding a thil nin hiaite ahi: buite, chikpite, thankikpi, a chi himhim,
english: “‘These are they which are unclean to you among the creeping things that creep on the earth: the weasel, the rat, any kind of great lizard,

paite: Innhik, tangteuh, thankik dokdawn leh zusa.
english: the gecko, and the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.

paite: Hiaite a vak a vak thoh chi tengteng lak a nou ding a thil ninte ahi uh: kuapeuh in a sisa hiaite a khoih uleh nitak lam tan in a nin ding uh.
english: These are they which are unclean to you among all that creep. Whoever touches them when they are dead, shall be unclean until the evening.

paite: Huan, a sih ua bangpeuh a delhkhum uh, a nin zel ding; vanzat photphot sing a bawl tui-um-belsuan hiam, puan hiam, savun hiam, sai-ip hiam leng hi hen aw, tui a diah ding ahi, huan, nitak lam tan in a nin ding; huai khit chiang in a siangthou ta ding hi.
english: On whatever any of them falls when they are dead, it shall be unclean; whether it is any vessel of wood, or clothing, or skin, or sack, whatever vessel it is, with which any work is done, it must be put into water, and it shall be unclean until the evening; then it will be clean.

paite: Leibel, a bang mahmah a kiakna peuhpeuh na hihtam zel ding uh ahi, a sung a om tengteng a nin ahi.
english: Every earthen vessel, into which any of them falls, all that is in it shall be unclean, and you shall break it.

paite: Huai bel a nek chi om tengteng leng huai a om tui a diahsa himhim, thil nin ahi ding; huan, dawn chi, dawn theih chi tengteng leng, huai bel a himhim zaw thil nin ahi ding.
english: All food which may be eaten, that on which water comes, shall be unclean; and all drink that may be drunk in every such vessel shall be unclean.

paite: Huan, thil bangpeuh a luang up a banglai peuh in a delhkhum sa photphot thil nin ahi zel ding; tanghou kanna hiam, kan lumna bel hiam leng hihtap vek ding ahi, a nin khin a, nou a ding in thil nin ahi ding.
english: Everything whereupon part of their carcass falls shall be unclean; whether oven, or range for pots, it shall be broken in pieces: they are unclean, and shall be unclean to you.

paite: Himahleh tuikhuk hiam, tuibem, tui chin khawm hiam a nin kei ding a, a luang uh sikkhak peuhmah a nin ding.
english: Nevertheless a spring or a cistern in which water is a gathered shall be clean: but that which touches their carcass shall be unclean.

paite: Huan, haichi, chin ding himhim zaw a luang uh a banglai peuh in na delhkhum ta leh, a nin kei.
english: If part of their carcass falls on any sowing seed which is to be sown, it is clean.

paite: Himahleh haichi, tui a diahsa a luang un a koilai peuh in delh leh, nou ding in thil nin ahi.
english: But if water is put on the seed, and part of their carcass falls on it, it is unclean to you.

paite: Gamsa na nek theih chi himhim u leng si leh, a luang khoih mi peuhmah nitak lam tan in a nin ding.
english: “‘If any animal, of which you may eat, dies; he who touches its carcass shall be unclean until the evening.

paite: A sa ne peuhmah in a puante uh sawp ding uh ahi, nitak lam tan in a nin ding: huan, a luang lami in leng a puante a sawp ding ahi, nitak lam tan in a nin ding.
english: He who eats of its carcass shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening. He also who carries its carcass shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening.

paite: Huan, ganhing leitung a a bok a vak chi tengteng thil kihhuai ahi ua, nek ding ahi kei.
english: “‘Every creeping thing that creeps on the earth is an abomination. It shall not be eaten.

paite: A tholh a kitholh chi leh khe li a pai chi hiam, khe tampi nei chi hiam, leitung a bok a vak chi himhim na ne ding uh ahi kei, thil kihhuai ahi ngal ua.
english: Whatever goes on its belly, and whatever goes on all fours, or whatever has many feet, even all creeping things that creep on the earth, them you shall not eat; for they are an abomination.

paite: A bok a vak chi himhim in na kihihthanghuai ding uh ahi kei, na kihihbuah louhna ding un, huaite in na kihihnin ding uh ahi kei.
english: You shall not make yourselves abominable with any creeping thing that creeps, neither shall you make yourselves unclean with them, that you should be defiled thereby.

paite: Kei zaw TOUPA na Pathian uh ka hi ngal a; huaiziak in kisiangthou sak unla, siangthou in om un; kei lah ka siangthou ngal a, leitung a teng, a bok a vak, a bang chi mah in kihihbuah kei un.
english: For I am Yahweh your God. Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be holy; for I am holy: neither shall you defile yourselves with any kind of creeping thing that moves on the earth.

paite: N Pathian uh hi ding a Aigupta gam a kipan a nou hon pikhia TOUPA lah ka hi ngal a: kei ka siangthou ngal a, huaiziak in nou leng na siangthou ding uh ahi.
english: For I am Yahweh who brought you up out of the land of Egypt, to be your God. You shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.

paite: Hiai pen gamsa leh vasate leh tui a teng chi thil hing chiteng leh lei a a bok a vak chi chitengte tungthu a dan ding ahi.Siangthou leh siangthoulou khenna ding leh, gamsa nek theih chi leh gamsa nek theihlouh chi khenna ding in, chi in, chi in.
english: “‘This is the law of the animal, and of the bird, and of every living creature that moves in the waters, and of every creature that creeps on the earth,

paite: Siangthou leh siangthoulou khenna ding leh, gamsa nek theih chi leh gamsa nek theihlouh chi khenna ding in, chi in, chi in.
english: to make a distinction between the unclean and the clean, and between the living thing that may be eaten and the living thing that may not be eaten.’”
